items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: That was the last time I saw Charlie Mingus

ctx.x: came all of this distance to play for money, and I don't know what you mean, that (you know what I mean) I gotta...that I'm not going to play if you can't come in....You know you gotta come in, if you come here to see me, you got to pay, 'cause they got to pay me." So that particular night we didn't play. So they had to postpone the thing 'til the next night.

The next night they had it in a big park. They must have had five hundred soldiers in that place. And they used to what clap (PRICE clapping). So/I...I figured out what I was going to do. I played me a Boogie-Woogie to that rhythm. I played a Boogie-Woogie to that rhythm. They (laughter) didn't understand what happened...I made my little exit and went about my business. That was the last time I saw Charlie Mingus, incidentally. Charlie was half sick, you know.

To play for 53 years and to continue to play make'me wonder how old I'm going to get. I don't know...I'm 71 now. I'm in my 72nd year. Maybe I'm going to follow Eubie Blake. I don't need my glasses to read...I don't use my glasses to read.
